subject: design/argus-write-hook
statement: The write-time deny is realized as a **per-CLI native pre-write hook** — each supported agent CLI's own pre-write hook surface, wired via configuration on the **vendor-neutral agent surface** with the canonical deny logic authored once and per-CLI adapters pointing at it (never forked content; AP-25) — each adapter set to **fail closed** *(design-brainstorm:argus-boundary-enforcement-tech-design#D-4, #ALT-6)*. The deny logic classifies the pending write's target against the protected-path set and the drive's declared scope, and **denies before any bytes are written**, returning a reason naming the path and the boundary. Where a supported CLI's hook defaults to fail-open, the adapter sets its fail-closed option explicitly; where a CLI exposes no honoring pre-write hook, that CLI is documented with the merge-boundary layers (parts 2+3) as its stated guarantee (UB-2). An **unresolvable declared scope ⇒ deny** (FR-2, AP-17); a **hook process error / crash / timeout ⇒ deny** (UB-6). An OS/container **sandbox** is deliberately **not** the mechanism — it needs privilege beyond the repo (a new operator-owned surface) and is unnecessary because the out-of-band guarantee belongs to the merge-boundary layers (§4, ABUSE-4).
